channel.description: Recent content in 2026-11 on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.117
item.description:
Release v1.0.117 adds sandbox CA certificate trust support, MCP/tool permission fixes, and several session/resume reliability improvements. It also fixes terminal/UI issues, permission prompt behavior, hooks/process handling, and model picker warnings.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: ECMP Nexthop
item.description:
Azure Virtual Network now supports ECMP routing in public preview. It lets customers use a single user-defined route to distribute traffic across 2 to 16 next hops.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Copilot code review billing will default to the organization
item.description:
If an organization has not selected a billing preference, Copilot code review for members with a Copilot license will start billing the organization by default on December 30, 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Java 8, 11 and 17 in Azure Functions ends on September 1, 2027
item.description:
Azure Functions will retire support for Java 8, 11, and 17 on September 1, 2027. Existing apps can keep running, but security updates and customer support for these Java versions will stop.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: What defenders need to know about ARTEX, the agentic AI framework threat actors abuse
item.description:
Microsoft says the AI-powered penetration testing framework ARTEX is being abused by multiple threat actors to speed up existing operations. The observed use cases include network reconnaissance, credential attacks, and web application exploitation.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Email Security
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Email Security for the second year in a row. The post provides no product changes or technical details.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.116
item.description:
Release 1.0.116 adds several CLI and editor integration fixes, including MCP/server startup and auth handling, sandbox and permissions behavior, session and model workflow improvements, and multiple terminal/UI accessibility corrections. It also includes changes for extension manifests, workspace MCP config parsing, search and diff edge cases, and memory growth reduction in long sessions.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: vscode: Visual Studio Code 1.148 (Insiders)
item.description:
Visual Studio Code 1.148 Insiders adds agent session management and editor tab improvements. The article is a release announcement for the latest Insiders build.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: dotnet: Introducing DocumentExtractionClient (preview): Extract documents in .NET
item.description:
Microsoft introduced DocumentExtractionClient, a preview .NET API for extracting structured content from PDFs, images, and other documents. The initial release includes starter providers to choose from.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Site Recovery support for zonal disaster recovery for Ultra disks
item.description:
Azure Site Recovery now supports Zone-to-Zone Disaster Recovery for Azure Ultra disks. This lets customers replicate and recover performance-intensive virtual machines across Availability Zones to handle zonal disruptions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: Choose the right stack for your AI application
item.description:
The article advises choosing the lowest abstraction layer that still lets you build the app, switch models, and use each model’s strongest features. It emphasizes avoiding unnecessary abstraction so you can adapt to model-specific capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Visual Studio November Update – Faster Workflows, Better Reviews
item.description:
The November Visual Studio update focuses on reducing repeated work in large solutions, adding MSBuild Restore support in Open Folder, and improving Copilot Chat with a new engine and work controls. It also adds tools for organizing large pull-request reviews plus CSS color previews and IntelliSense.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Optimize agents from insights in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Optimization from insights is now in public preview in Foundry Agent Service. From an eligible prompt-agent trace in the Foundry portal, users can generate and evaluate candidate changes to an agent’s instructions and function-calling tool descriptions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Govern MCP tools with your own gateway in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service now supports public preview for routing MCP tool traffic through organization-managed AI Gateway or Azure API Management endpoints. The MCP route is configured in the gateway first, then used by the agent service.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Use Azure Storage permissions in Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ
item.description:
Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ now support Azure Storage permissions to control access to search results. When configured, search apps and AI agents return only content each user is allowed to access.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Native A2A passthrough for hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Agent Service now supports native A2A passthrough for hosted agents in public preview, letting existing Agent2Agent agents connect without a protocol conversion layer. Incoming A2A requests are forwarded directly instead of being converted to the Responses protocol.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Developer CLI extension for Azure Document Intelligence and Content Understanding in Foundry Tools
item.description:
A public preview Azure Developer CLI extension adds azd ai cu commands for analyzing documents with Azure Document Intelligence and Content Understanding in Microsoft Foundry Tools. It can save analysis results as Markdown or JSON.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Cost controls for model and agent spending in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now supports cost controls for model and agent spending in public preview. Users can set spending or token budgets for a Foundry resource or project, with alerts sent via Azure Event Grid or new requests blocked when the threshold is reached.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Central governance of hosted-agent outbound domains in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Azure Policy can now govern outbound destinations for hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service. Agent authors must attach a compliant egress policy before creating an agent version, and that policy controls outbound requests.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: More predictable notifications on GitHub.com
item.description:
GitHub.com notifications will be migrated starting December 1, 2026, over the course of a week. The change is intended to make subscriptions more predictable, fix unexpected behavior, and support higher activity scale.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry | Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Ignite 2026 introduces updates across agents, developer tools, models, training, enterprise context, and governance. The post also emphasizes continuous improvement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.115
item.description:
Release v1.0.115 adds many CLI fixes and UI/layout improvements, plus new model and provider support. It also tightens sandbox, MCP, permissions, session-resume, and background-process handling across macOS, Windows, and Unix.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: visualstudio: Beyond the prompt: Discovering trusted technical perspectives with your Visual Studio subscription
item.description:
The post says AI can speed up code generation, but developers still need to verify security, reliability, and maintainability. It introduces trusted technical perspectives available through a Visual Studio subscription to help validate AI-assisted work.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Enterprise Knowledge Graph in Foundry IQ
item.description:
Foundry IQ now supports Enterprise Knowledge Graph as a knowledge source in public preview. It extracts entities and relationships from unstructured content during indexing, using a user-provided ontology.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Updated Guardrails experience in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Guardrails now exposes an updated experience in public preview for configuring agent runtime safety controls. It includes classifiers, deterministic rules, and LLM-based judges, and surfaces required controls when administrator policy enforces them.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: IQ Retriever Zero in Foundry IQ
item.description:
Foundry IQ now supports IQ Retriever Zero in public preview. It uses an iterative retrieval approach to split complex questions into focused searches, review results, and search again within a configured budget before passing evidence to the answering model.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Public Preview: Style and instruction control for HD V3 voices in Azure Speech in Foundry Tools
item.description:
Azure Speech in Foundry Tools now offers HD V3 voices with style and instruction control in public preview. The feature is intended for shaping voice delivery in voice agents, narration, and other speech experiences.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Human annotation for agent evaluations in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Human annotation for agent evaluations is now in public preview in Microsoft Foundry. Reviewers can add ratings, tags, comments, and expected outputs to agent traces for evaluation workflows.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Agent insights in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now provides agent insights that analyze agent traces to identify recurring patterns and group related issues. Users can review an insight with its supporting traces, then use agent optimizer to test potential fixes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Files knowledge source for Foundry IQ
item.description:
Foundry IQ now supports a managed Files knowledge source in general availability. You can upload files directly for processing and indexing without setting up a storage account or scheduled indexer.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Issue statuses and repository boards are in public preview
item.description:
GitHub added more specific issue statuses and repository boards in public preview, giving teams shared context beyond just open or closed. The feature is meant to show where an issue stands and help track work in flight.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Call model router without a deployment in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now supports calling the model router directly, without creating a deployment first. In supported regions, you can set the model to auto in Responses or Chat Completions requests to use Balanced routing by default.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Use the Messages API with model router in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Model router in Microsoft Foundry now supports the Messages API in public preview. This lets messages-based apps and coding tools use automatic model selection while preserving the Anthropic request and response format.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Use your model deployments with model router in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Model router in Microsoft Foundry now supports using your existing model deployments for routed requests in public preview. This lets you reuse existing capacity while the router chooses a model per request.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Model router now supports the Responses API protocol in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s model router now supports the Responses API protocol in general availability on both resource and project endpoints. Applications using Responses can point to the model router deployment name to enable automatic model selection.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Use model router with AI Gateway
item.description:
Azure AI Gateway now supports a model router in public preview for automatic model selection. For each request, it ranks models behind an alias using Microsoft Foundry, then combines that ranking with alias priorities and weights to choose a backend.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Deploy hosted agents from your own container registry in Foundry Toolkit for VS Code
item.description:
Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code now supports deploying hosted agents from prebuilt images stored in customer-managed container registries, not just Azure Container Registry. Users select the corresponding registry connection in their Foundry project.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Wildcard domain support in Azure Firewall network rules
item.description:
Azure Firewall network rules now support wildcard domains in FQDN-based rules and are generally available. Customers can use patterns such as *.contoso.com to simplify rule management.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Secret scanning reduces false positives for Slack
item.description:
GitHub updated secret scanning to reduce false positives for Slack incoming webhook URLs. The detector now excludes certain URLs to cut down on incorrect matches.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure AI Content Safety selected features will be retired on April 30, 2027
item.description:
Azure AI Content Safety will retire several preview capabilities on April 30, 2027. The retired items include Analyze Multimodal, custom categories (rapid) for text and image, and connected/disconnected containers for Text, Image, and Prompt Shields.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL enhanced Burstable tier (Basv2)
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL now has a public preview of the enhanced Burstable tier (Basv2). It keeps the burstable model but adds improved performance predictability and more efficient burst utilization for steadier, lower-cost workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Run local models in your .NET apps with Llama on Windows
item.description:
Microsoft describes how to run local Llama models on Windows from a .NET app using downloads from Hugging Face and the llama.cpp team. The example uses a .NET 11 C# file-based app to load an open model and call it locally.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: WAF Insights for Azure Front Door
item.description:
WAF Insights is now generally available for Azure Front Door Web Application Firewall (WAF). It adds built-in dashboards in the WAF policy that combine logs and metrics for investigating blocked requests.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.38 Sneak Peek
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.38 is previewing several removals and behavior changes, including kubectl WebSocket opt-out env var removal, kuberc API cleanup, cgroup v1 phaseout, admission webhook filtering for authn/authz review resources, and stricter cgroup driver discovery from container runtimes. Planned upgrades include kuberc and pod-level resources reaching stable, DRA partitionable devices stabilizing, and a new alpha EvictionRequest API.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Code coverage uploads now flag invalid report formats
item.description:
The GitHub Code Quality upload-code-coverage action now validates that uploaded coverage reports are in Cobertura XML format. If the report is in an unsupported format, the upload step now fails.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Usage reports will include a user ID column starting December 1
item.description:
Starting December 1, 2026, GitHub usage reports that include a username column will also include a user_id column beside it. Columns after username will shift one position to the right.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Hosted agents in your own virtual network: five checks when the Agents page times out
item.description:
The article explains five common checks for using hosted agents in a private virtual network, focusing on subnet selection, Agents page timeouts, TLS-inspecting firewalls, VNet peering and DNS, and why a subnet may remain in use after an account is deleted.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Governance policy guidance in Foundry Canvas and VS Code
item.description:
Governance policy guidance is now generally available in Foundry Canvas and the Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code. As agents are built, both surfaces show relevant policies for agent types, models, toolboxes, and guardrails, including warnings.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Microsoft Copilot harness support in Foundry Toolkit for VS Code
item.description:
Agent Builder in Microsoft Foundry Toolkit for VS Code now supports prompt agents using the Microsoft Copilot harness in public preview. Developers can configure tools and skills, edit local YAML definitions, deploy changes to Foundry, and run the agents.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Azure Functions OpenAI Extension ends on April 20, 2027
item.description:
Support for the Azure Functions OpenAI extension ends on April 20, 2027. Users should migrate to the appropriate direct SDKs before that date, including OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, or Azure AI Search SDKs depending on the scenario.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Programmed Training in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Programmed Training is now in public preview in Microsoft Foundry. It provides an API for building custom post-training loops over open-weight models, with access available by request through a preview sign-up form.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Multi-turn evaluation in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now offers multi-turn evaluation in public preview. It lets you assess full agent conversations against quality standards instead of evaluating only individual responses.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Security advisory permissions are now generally available
item.description:
GitHub now supports using custom repository roles to grant access for working on repository security advisories, including private vulnerability reports. This removes the need to make users repository administrators just for advisory work.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 release candidate
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 is available as a release candidate. The post says it adds new capabilities across the platform and mentions updates to GitHub Projects, but does not provide specifics in the excerpt.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Firewall for Containers
item.description:
Azure Firewall for Containers is in public preview. It extends Azure Firewall protections to containerized workloads so network traffic for container environments can be secured and managed centrally.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: AI is Changing the Cross-Platform Decision Matrix
item.description:
The post says AI agents can now rebuild a .NET MAUI app using platform-specific UI in days, which changes the tradeoffs between cross-platform and native approaches. It focuses on the build cost, maintenance cost, and runtime implications of that choice.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: commandline: Iteratively improving public benchmarks
item.description:
The article states that it audits two coding benchmarks: DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench 4.0. No further details are provided in the supplied content.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM
item.description:
Microsoft says it was recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SIEM. The post contains no additional product details, features, or release information.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: ai: Serve open models in production with Foundry Managed Compute
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Managed Compute is now generally available for serving open models in production on dedicated GPUs. It supports Global and US or EU Data Zone deployments.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Pin your favorite repositories to your dashboard
item.description:
GitHub added a Favorite repositories section on the Dashboard so you can choose which repositories appear there. If the new dashboard experience is not enabled, the existing Top repositories section stays the same.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Desktop now supports multiple accounts per host
item.description:
GitHub Desktop now supports signing in with multiple accounts on the same host. This works for GitHub.com, GitHub Enterprise Server, and GHE.com.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Improvements on the pull request overview in public preview
item.description:
GitHub updated the pull request Overview page in public preview with clearer merge status and more explicit next steps. The changes are based on feedback since the November 5, 2026 preview release.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Announcing: Multiparty private offers in Microsoft Marketplace expands to Malaysia and Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Multiparty private offers in Microsoft Marketplace now support Malaysia and Saudi Arabia. This lets partners procure third-party cloud and AI solutions for customers in those markets through Marketplace.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Soft delete in Azure Compute Gallery
item.description:
Soft delete for Azure Compute Gallery is now generally available. Deleted image versions can be recovered within a configurable retention period of 7 to 365 days, and deployments can still use soft-deleted images during that period.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: PostgreSQL 19 on Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server now supports PostgreSQL 19 in public preview in the East Asia region. You can provision new PostgreSQL 19 servers via the Azure portal and Azure CLI.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: visualstudio: Live technical training, wherever you are: A VSLive! benefit for Visual Studio subscribers
item.description:
Microsoft announced a VSLive! benefit for Visual Studio subscribers: live technical training accessible wherever they are. The post frames this as a way to build AI tool skills through structured learning beyond docs and tutorials.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Zone resilience for Azure VMs
item.description:
Zone resilience for Azure VMs is in public preview. It allows an eligible zonal VM to be recovered in another availability zone within the same region while keeping the existing VM resource and configuration, with ZRS managed disks used for synchronous cross-zone replication.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: Build trusted autonomous agents for your team with Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry announces guidance for building trusted autonomous agents for teams, framing the problem as trust and governance rather than raw agent capability.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Enterprise Live Migrations from Azure DevOps generally available
item.description:
Enterprise Live Migrations from Azure DevOps Services to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency are now generally available. The feature lets organizations migrate repositories while teams continue working.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Red Hat Enterprise Linux runner images now generally available
item.description:
Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 images for GitHub-hosted larger runners are now generally available. They were previously in public preview starting in June 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Database Agent for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Public preview of Database Agent for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. The feature monitors database health proactively and helps detect, understand, and respond to performance and health issues faster.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: S3 audit log streaming with OpenID Connect expands to GHE.com
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (GHE.com) now supports streaming enterprise audit logs to Amazon S3 using OpenID Connect (OIDC). This brings the same S3 audit log streaming capability previously available on github.com to GHE.com.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Wait for pull request events with GitHub CLI
item.description:
GitHub CLI v2.105.0 adds support for GitHub Event Streams, allowing you to wait for pull request events with a single command instead of polling. The update is aimed at both users and agents monitoring PR changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Connect Supabase, Box, Calendly, and more to Copilot
item.description:
GitHub added public preview support for connecting eight additional services to Copilot through GitHub-verified MCP servers (connectors). These join the more than 25 services already available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for agentic coding, multistep tool use, and knowledge work.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: AI bot ruleset for Azure Front Door Premium WAF
item.description:
Azure Front Door Premium WAF now has a public preview AI bot ruleset. It lets you control access for AI crawlers and agents, complementing robots.txt for finer-grained traffic handling.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: The new Azure Databricks on Azure Government is now in Beta
item.description:
Azure Databricks is now available in Beta on Microsoft Azure Government. It provides the Databricks data and AI platform for U.S. public sector agencies and partners as a first-party Azure service.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Cross-subscription backup for Azure Virtual Machines in Azure Backup
item.description:
Azure Backup now supports cross-subscription backup for Azure Virtual Machines. You can protect VMs with a Recovery Services vault in a different Azure subscription, as long as it is in the same tenant.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: AI-powered application and database modernization with Modernize CLI
item.description:
Modernize CLI is in public preview for AI-assisted application and database modernization. It assesses application architecture, dependencies, cloud readiness, and the databases an application uses to guide modernization as a connected workflow.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026: from pilot to production inside your enterprise boundaries
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service added enterprise-focused hosted agent capabilities at Ignite 2026, including shared subnet IPs, private CA trust, network egress controls, deployment to customer-managed AKS clusters, resilient execution, and memory snapshots.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Browser Automation Tool in Microsoft Foundry : Ignite’26 Announcements
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry announced a browser automation tool for agents with enterprise-focused controls and browser session features. The update adds MCP action batching, Live View with Take control, session recording, VNet injection, browser proxy, profile reuse, secret management, and CAPTCHA handling.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: The Foundry Dev Pack is here: build Foundry agents your way
item.description:
Microsoft has made the Foundry Dev Pack generally available. It installs Microsoft Foundry developer tools locally in one package so you can build agents from an editor, terminal, or coding agent.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: What’s new in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft announces Ignite 2026 updates for Foundry Agent Service, focused on making agents more reliable in production by improving context handling, tool use, runtime resilience, and iterative improvement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Build once, reuse across your agent fleet: Tools and Toolboxes in Foundry
item.description:
The post introduces Tools and Toolboxes in Foundry as a way to share agent capabilities across multiple production agents instead of wiring the same integrations separately for each one. It focuses on reducing duplicated instructions, dependencies, and setup work when scaling agent fleets.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: vscode: Visual Studio Code 1.147 (Insiders)
item.description:
The provided content only states that Visual Studio Code 1.147 (Insiders) is available and links to the full article. No release-note details are included in the supplied text.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: github: Security risk assessments run automatically on GitHub Team
item.description:
GitHub now runs security risk assessments automatically for organizations on GitHub Team. Admins and security managers can review free assessment findings to identify exposed credentials and code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Introducing agent controls: An enterprise control plane for agent behavior
item.description:
Microsoft introduced agent controls, a managed Azure service for applying runtime policy to enterprise agents. It is built on the open-source Agent Control Specification (ACS) and Agent Hooks.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Customize GitHub Copilot for your team
item.description:
GitHub Copilot team customizations are now generally available for organization teams. Teams can share Copilot plugins they rely on so members do not need to repeat the same setup.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.114
item.description:
Release 1.0.114 contains fixes and changes. No additional details are provided in the release note body.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Immutable snapshots for Azure Disk Storage
item.description:
Immutable snapshots for Azure Disk Storage are now in public preview. They complement Azure Backup immutable vaults by providing a short-term backup option with faster recovery characteristics.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Azure Boost observability for NVMe disks
item.description:
Azure Boost observability for NVMe disks is an open-source CLI tool for compatible Azure VMs. It reports remote disk I/O and latency metrics and maps each in-VM disk to the corresponding disk.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: vscode: The Copilot harness: Building on a shared foundation
item.description:
VS Code says it is moving from the Local harness to the Copilot harness. The change is based on usage data and user feedback, but the provided text does not include implementation details or timelines.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: azure: Generally Available: Cobalt 200 Arm-based Dplsv7, Dpsv7, Epsv7, Mpsv4, and Lpsv5-series Virtual Machines
item.description:
Azure has made Cobalt 200 Arm-based VM series generally available across several SKUs, including Dpsv7/Dplsv7, Epsv7, Mpsv4, and Lpsv5. The update says these VMs improve on the previous Cobalt 100 generation.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Intel and AMD v6 with temp disk for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is now generally available on Intel and AMD v6 compute tiers with local temporary disk. The new generation adds higher performance and larger scale options to the Flexible Server portfolio.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Intel and AMD v5 diskless tier for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now generally available on Intel and AMD v5 diskless compute. The new General Purpose and Memory Optimized SKUs do not include local temporary storage.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Cobalt 200 compute for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now generally available on Cobalt 200, a Microsoft-designed ARM64 compute option. It expands the Flexible Server compute portfolio with an additional architecture choice.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Geo-redundant backup and restore for Azure HorizonDB
item.description:
Geo-redundant backup and restore is now generally available for Azure HorizonDB. It lets you store backups in a geo-redundant way and restore a HorizonDB deployment in another Azure region when needed.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Generally Available: Customize backup retention from 1 to 35 days in Azure HorizonDB
item.description:
Azure HorizonDB backup retention can now be configured from 1 to 35 days. This lets deployments match retention settings to application and data protection requirements.

  • Source: Azure Updates
